title: Dimension-zero diagonal/deformation orientation and tensor-map normalization
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated etale morphism of finite type between Noetherian schemes (schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) on which $\ell$ is invertible. Assume $f$ is compactifiable [def-asd-compactifiable]. Work in the ordinary etale derived categories of constant $A$-module sheaves. Write $f_A^\times$ for the right adjoint of $Rf_{!,A}$ and $\omega_f=f_A^\times A_Y$. Identify this adjunction with the etale sum-extension adjunction $Df_{\Sigma!}\dashv f^*$, including its sum counit, using the canonical proper-support comparison of [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], with its graph normalization and specified-map compatibilities of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility]. Put $W=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$, diagonal $\Delta$ and rank-zero normal bundle $\pi:N_\Delta=X\to X$ with zero section $z=1_X$. Form $\alpha_f:\omega_f\to A_X$ as the composite of (i) $\Delta^*$ of the exceptional base-change isomorphism $p_2^*\omega_f\to\omega_{p_1}$ [prop-asd-smooth-base-change], (ii) the normalized deformation comparison $\delta_{p_1,\Delta}$ [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization], and (iii) $z^*$ of the inverse vector-bundle purity isomorphism [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity], with the rank-zero integration of [def-amb-vector-integration]. Under the above adjunction-preserving identifications, each factor, and hence $\alpha_f$, is the identity of $A_X$. For every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, let $\phi_{f,K}:f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\to f_A^\times K$ be the canonical projection-and-counit tensor map of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. Then
$$\phi_{f,K}\circ(1\otimes\alpha_f^{-1}):f^*K\longrightarrow f_A^\times K$$
is the canonical comparison of right adjoints preserving the sum counit. In particular its adjoint $Rf_{!,A}f^*K\to K$ is exactly the sum/evaluation counit.

source.place: Three-factor purity formula, specialized to relative dimension zero; returned item Step 7 expands the etale sum-counit normalization

proof.text:
Fix the following normalization for any separated finite-type etale map $e:V\to T$ between Noetherian schemes and a compactification $c$. Write $F_e=Re_!$, $S_e=D(e_{\Sigma!})$. The canonical comparison $c_e:F_e\xrightarrow{\sim}S_e$ exists on the whole unbounded category by [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact]. We use its graph-normalized comparison, exactly the $c_e^c$ of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility], not an arbitrary functor isomorphism. The sum adjunction $S_e\dashv e^*$ is [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], and $F_e\dashv e^\times$ is [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The Hom bijections send $a:F_eM\to K$ first to $a c_e(M)^{-1}:S_eM\to K$, then to its sum-adjoint. They give the unique natural isomorphism $\rho_{e,K}:e^\times K\to e^*K$ satisfying
$$\epsilon^c_{e,K}=\epsilon^\Sigma_{e,K}\,c_e(e^*K)\,F_e(\rho_{e,K}).$$
Indeed start with the counit, which corresponds to the identity of $e^\times K$ under the first adjunction; naturality then gives the displayed counit equation. The inverse Hom bijections and the triangle identities give its inverse. This specifies the adjunction-preserving coordinates, including $\omega_e\cong A_V$.

source.place: Three-factor finite purity formula and its relative-dimension-zero normalization, expanded by the agent using the Stacks graph and projection maps

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1) to $f$ along $f$: $p_1:W=X\times_YX\to X$ is etale. It is separated and finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], and $W$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], both $f$ and $p_1$ are smooth of pure relative dimension zero. The diagonal is a section of $p_1$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion] shows it is an isomorphism onto an open and closed component $\Delta(X)\subset W$. Thus $W=\Delta(X)\amalg V_0$ with $V_0$ open and closed. The regular-immersion assertion [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion] supplies regular codimension zero and normal rank zero; equivalently the ideal is zero on $\Delta(X)$ and the whole structure sheaf on $V_0$, so $\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2=0$, $N_\Delta=X$ and $\pi=z=1_X$.

proof.text:
We compute exceptional base change in the coordinates of Step 1. For a square with etale vertical map $e$, write $h:V'\to V$, $g:T'\to T$, $e':V'\to T'$, and $\chi:h^*e^*\cong e'^*g^*$. By [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility](1), the actual proper/open exchange $C:g^*F_e\to F_{e'}h^*$ becomes the specified sum exchange $b:g^*S_e\to S_{e'}h^*$. Its inverse is the conjugate defined in [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]. That conjugate's unit--exchange--counit formula, with the two triangle identities, gives
$$g^*\epsilon^\Sigma_{e,K}\circ b_{e^*K}^{-1}=\epsilon^\Sigma_{e',g^*K}\circ S_{e'}(\chi_K).\tag{E}$$
Concretely the underived exchange is the restriction identification of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-underived-exchange-restriction]; both composites evaluate the section on the pulled-back lift. This is an equality of sheaf maps, hence degreewise of complexes, and of their descended maps for the exact sum and inverse-image functors. Substituting (E) and the counit equation of Step 1 into the defining transpose $g^*\epsilon^c\circ C^{-1}$ of [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] shows that $\beta_{e,g,K}$ becomes precisely $\chi_K$. For $K=A_T$ it is the unit identification $h^*A_V\to A_{V'}$. Applying this to $e=f$, $g=f$, and pulling back by $\Delta$ proves that the first factor of $\alpha_f$ is the identity in these coordinates.

proof.text:
Compute the rank-zero deformation directly from its definition in [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization]. On $\Delta(X)$ the ideal is zero, so the Rees subalgebra is $\mathcal O_X[t]$. On $V_0$ it is $\mathcal O_{V_0}$, so adjoining $\mathcal I/t$ adjoins $t^{-1}$, and the algebra is $\mathcal O_{V_0}[t,t^{-1}]$. The two pieces are disjoint open and closed pieces of $W$, so these calculations give
$$D=\mathbf A^1_X\amalg(V_0\times\mathbf G_m),$$
with $\widetilde g$ equal to the identity on the first component and to the restriction of $p_1\times1$ on the second. The deformed section is the inclusion of the first component. The fibre at $1$ is $W$ with section $\Delta$; at $0$ only the first component remains, giving $(X,1_X)$. These identifications send $t$ to the base parameter and preserve the section; they are the fibre identifications of the defining Rees algebra.

proof.text: Here are the hypotheses for the specialization theorem, before using its conclusion. The component $V_0$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The map $\widetilde g$ in Step 4 is etale: on the first component it is the identity, and on the second it is the base change of $p_1$ followed by restriction to an open subscheme, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. It is separated and finite type: $W\times\mathbf A^1\to\mathbf A^1_X$ has these properties by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; the displayed $D$ is its open subscheme obtained by deleting $V_0\times\{0\}$. Restriction preserves the locally finite-type affine presentations, and quasi-compactness follows from the Noetherian open-subscheme lemma. Its relative diagonal is the restriction of the ambient closed diagonal, hence is closed. The ambient scheme and $\mathbf A^1_X$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and $D$ is Noetherian by the open-subscheme lemma. All have $\ell$ invertible by pullback. Noetherian schemes are quasi-compact by definition and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Therefore [thm-nagata-compactification] applies to $p_1$, $\widetilde g$ and $\pi=1_X$. They are compactifiable. Etaleness gives smooth relative dimension zero by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and Step 2 gives the required regular closed section.

proof.text: Apply the coordinates of Step 1 to the three etale maps $p_1$, $\widetilde g$ and $\pi$. Thus $C=\Delta^*\omega_{p_1}=A_X$ and $F=\widetilde\Delta^*\omega_{\widetilde g}=A_{\mathbf A^1_X}$. Step 3 at the inclusions $t=1,0$ says that the canonical exceptional fibre comparisons are the identity unit comparisons. Consequently the identity $A_{\mathbf A^1_X}\to a^*A_X$ is an isomorphism $F\to a^*C$ whose fibre at $1$ is $1_C$ under exactly the specified fibre maps. The uniqueness clause of [lem-pur-noetherian-etale-section-specialization] forces $\kappa_{p_1,\Delta}$ to be this map. Restricting at $0$ and inverting proves $\delta_{p_1,\Delta}=1_{A_X}$. No assertion about an unspecified locality isomorphism is used to determine this scalar.

proof.text: For $\pi=1_X$, the rank-zero clause of [def-amb-vector-integration] prescribes the identity adjunction trace. By [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity], the vector-bundle purity map at $A_X$ is its adjoint. Under Step 1, the identity morphism's compact-support comparison is the identity by [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], its projection map is the tensor-unit map by [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility](2), and its sum adjunction is the identity adjunction. The adjoint of the rank-zero trace is therefore $1_{A_X}$. Its inverse and zero-section pullback are also identities. Together with Steps 3 and 6 this proves every factor of $\alpha_f$ is the identity, or, before changing coordinates, $\alpha_f=\rho_{f,A_Y}$.

proof.text:
We now identify the actual projection map in the tensor transpose of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor]. For a chosen compactification $c=(j,r)$, let $P^c_{f,M,K}$ and $p^\Sigma_{f,M,K}$ be exactly the proper-counit/open-tensor and sum-extension maps of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility](2). The projection in [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition] is constructed from exactly that proper projection and open-extension tensor map, with the two tensor factors switched to put $f^*K$ first; hence its inverse is the projection in the defining transpose of $\phi$. In the notation $Q$ for its inverse in this order, that lemma's equality, inverted and conjugated by the natural tensor symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym], gives
$$(1_K\otimes c_f(M))\,Q^c_{K,M}=Q^\Sigma_{K,M}\,c_f(f^*K\otimes^L M).\tag{P}$$
This follows by multiplying $c_f P^c=p^\Sigma(c_f\otimes1)$ on either side by the inverse projections and then applying the two switches. Thus it concerns the specified compactification projection, not a map chosen from its endpoints.

source.place: Three-factor finite purity formula and its relative-dimension-zero normalization, expanded by the agent using the Stacks graph and projection maps

proof.text:
Let $v_K=\phi_{f,K}(1\otimes\alpha_f^{-1})$, inserting the tensor-unit isomorphism $f^*K\cong f^*K\otimes A_X$. By the defining transpose in [thm-asd-smooth-tensor], its adjoint is $\lambda(1_K\otimes\epsilon^c_{f,A_Y})Q^c_{K,\omega_f}F_f(1\otimes\alpha_f^{-1})$. Naturality of the projection moves $\alpha_f^{-1}$ through $Q^c$. The counit equation of Step 1 and Step 7 give $\epsilon^c_{f,A_Y}F_f(\alpha_f^{-1})=\epsilon^\Sigma_{f,A_Y}c_f(A_X)$. Substituting (P) therefore identifies this adjoint with
$$\lambda(1_K\otimes\epsilon^\Sigma_{f,A_Y})Q^\Sigma_{K,A_X}\,c_f(f^*K).\tag{T}$$
The first three maps equal $\epsilon^\Sigma_{f,K}$. Indeed the generator formula of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility](2) sends $(s,k_s\otimes a)$ through the inverse projection and evaluation to $a k_s$ in $K$, exactly the sum/evaluation counit from $S_f\dashv f^*$ [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. This is a sheaf-map identity on the sheafified lift-indexed sums [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], degreewise for any complex representing $K$. It computes the derived maps: $A_X$ is flat in degree zero, and its sum extension is K-flat by [lem-pur-etale-sum-flat-kflat]. There is no sign from the degree-zero factor. Thus (T) is exactly $\epsilon^\Sigma_{f,K}c_f(f^*K)$. The bijection for $F_f\dashv f^\times$ now makes $v_K=\rho_{f,K}^{-1}$, the unique adjunction-preserving comparison of Step 1. This proves the specified-map and adjoint clauses for every unbounded $K$.

lean.note: The three named geometric factors are compared separately in graph-normalized adjunction coordinates. The comparison family is universally quantified with exactly the graph and homotopy normalization equations of lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility. No existence theorem from lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization is used. The actual Rees cone is transported to its rank-zero identity representative by its projection and zero section; its inverse purity factor uses the identity-adjunction trace prescribed by def-amb-vector-integration at rank zero. All auxiliary declarations belong to this construction; there is one postponed theorem.
